decision_completion.question: Do users who start a purchase judgment finish one, and does it change what they do?

preview_usefulness.question: After seeing a preview, does the user act on the decision — and when the preview cannot be shown, does the decision still carry them?

repeat_use.question: Do users come back to the decision flow on another day?

hidden_quality_rate.question: How often is a generated preview withheld from the user, and is that the quality gate working or the provider failing?

latency.question: How long does a decision take, and does asking for a preview slow it down?

cost_per_useful_decision.question: What does one decision that actually changed behavior cost in paid generations?

visual_trust.question: Do users recognize themselves, and do they say the garment came out wrong?

consent_cost.question: Does asking for a photo cost us decisions, and who agrees to it?

6.reason: Users mistaking the preview for a size guarantee is a comprehension failure; only moderated sessions and support/review reports can detect it.

8.reason: Being clearly worse than comparable products a user has already seen is a relative judgment with no in-app referent; requires benchmark review.

10.reason: Sacrificing Today and import-to-first-outfit is a program-allocation judgment, not a user-behavior signal in this contract.

pipeline_prerequisites.requirement: A frozen event contract shared by both repos.
pipeline_prerequisites.detail: V3-002: 11 events, a 5-field envelope and 15 metrics, byte-identical in aidrobe-BE and aidrobe-FE.

pipeline_prerequisites.requirement: An emitter for every event, on the side the contract declares as owner.
pipeline_prerequisites.detail: All 11 events are emitted: the 4 be-owned ones through app/common/analytics_emit.py, the 7 fe-owned ones through trackV3. Asserted by the emitter-coverage tests on both sides.

pipeline_prerequisites.requirement: A sink that persists emitted events somewhere queryable.
pipeline_prerequisites.detail: BE emits through structlog into application logs — no schema, no retention guarantee, not queryable as events. FE never calls setAnalyticsDispatcher, so the 7 fe-owned events reach a __DEV__ console.log and nothing at all in a release build. This is the single reason the dashboard has no numbers, and it is the largest one.

pipeline_prerequisites.requirement: V3 flags enabled for a cohort, so events are produced at all.
pipeline_prerequisites.detail: All three ENABLE_V3_* flags are False in committed configuration on both sides. This prerequisite is deliberately unmet — V3-023 acceptance 3 requires it.

readiness_gates.statement: The internal quality gate passes at a rate that can be operated stably.
evidence: V3-018 implemented the gate and the no-result fallback
readiness_gates.blocker: The pass RATE is a property of a real provider's output. Every run so far used the fake adapter, which composites a stub instead of generating, so no rate observed here predicts a production one.

readiness_gates.statement: Most seed users say the render basically looks like them.
readiness_gates.blocker: Needs real photos, a real provider and seed users. identity_fidelity_rate is defined and has no data.

readiness_gates.statement: Most seed users find garment color and overall silhouette believable.
readiness_gates.blocker: Same as above; garment_fidelity_complaint_rate is defined and has no data.

readiness_gates.statement: Obvious body beautification, age drift or garment deformation is very rare.
readiness_gates.blocker: No metric can carry this — the contract forbids body inferences as event fields by design, so it is a benchmark-review judgment on real provider output.

readiness_gates.statement: An avatar-ready user reaches a preview with at most one extra explicit action.
evidence: V3-022 FE driver shot 06 — one tap, render on screen, decision still under it

readiness_gates.statement: A user with no avatar still completes the purchase judgment in full.
evidence: V3-022 FE driver shots 01-02 — zero assets, zero try-on jobs, setup offered not required

readiness_gates.statement: A failed preview does not reduce decision-flow completion.
evidence: V3-022 FE driver shots 03/04/05 — byte-identical frames across failure, rejection and unknown status
readiness_gates.blocker: Proven: the decision SURVIVES a failure. Not proven: that failures do not depress the completion rate in the field. The declared metric for that is fallback_decision_retention_rate on the preview_usefulness panel, which joins v3_preview_viewed[result=fallback] to v3_decision_action on flow_id and needs data. Stated precisely, because it bounds what this dashboard can answer: the decision_completion panel CANNOT be segmented by preview outcome — its own events (v3_decision_started/completed/action) carry no generation_status, and declaring such a segment would fail test_every_segment_by_field_resolves_within_its_panel. A true completion-rate-with-failure vs without comparison therefore needs a cross-panel flow join that no single panel declares; the retention rate is the honest single-panel answer.

readiness_gates.statement: The user clearly understands this is not a size guarantee.
evidence: V3-020 renders the §22 boundary sentence on every preview
V3_SPEC §21 forbids a fit score, and none is implemented
readiness_gates.blocker: Shipping the sentence is not evidence of comprehension. §20.6 is qualitative-only by V3-002's own declaration: only moderated sessions or support reports can detect this.

readiness_gates.statement: Most users say the preview increased their purchase or wearing confidence.
readiness_gates.blocker: A stated-preference question no in-app event answers. Needs the Phase 1 qualitative study.

readiness_gates.statement: It confirms, changes or vetoes a decision rather than being merely entertaining.
readiness_gates.blocker: post_preview_decision_action_rate is defined precisely for this and has no data. This is the metric §20.3 would be killed on.

readiness_gates.statement: Users find it more helpful than single-garment try-on on shopping platforms.
readiness_gates.blocker: §20.8 is qualitative-only by V3-002's declaration: a relative judgment with no in-app referent. Needs benchmark review against products the user has already seen.

readiness_gates.statement: There is observable intent to use it again.
readiness_gates.blocker: repeat_use_rate is defined and has no data.

readiness_gates.statement: The cache hits effectively for a repeated garment/avatar combination.
evidence: tests/api/test_v3_e2e_journeys.py::test_an_avatar_ready_user_reaches_a_cached_preview_with_one_action — a second create POST returns the same asset_id and adds no job row
V3-017 idempotent async jobs keyed on a stable combination key

readiness_gates.statement: The static-image pass rate and the cost per useful decision are inside budget.
readiness_gates.blocker: Two missing inputs, not one: there is no provider price (so COST_MODEL's unit price is null) and no budget to compare against.

readiness_gates.statement: Video or multi-view is not a P0 prerequisite.
evidence: V3_SPEC §21 defers 360° video and multi-preview menus
No feature in feature_list.json implements either; the try-on port is static-only (V3-016)

seed_study.question: Do users understand how this differs from single-garment try-on on a shopping platform?
seed_study.what_to_observe: Unprompted, whether the user describes it as a whole-outfit judgment against their own wardrobe rather than as a garment fitting — and whether they read the §22 boundary sentence as a caveat or as a size promise.
discharges: Users find it more helpful than single-garment try-on on shopping platforms.
The user clearly understands this is not a size guarantee.

seed_study.question: Are users willing to authorize a photo, and where do they stop?
seed_study.what_to_observe: The point at which a user declines: the ask itself, the consent copy, or the photo capture. Declining is a valid outcome — the no-avatar path must stay complete.

seed_study.question: At which moment do users most want the preview?
seed_study.what_to_observe: Where in the flow the user asks for it unprompted, and whether they ever want it BEFORE reading the text decision — which would contradict the on-demand design.

seed_study.question: Does the preview change or confirm a purchase decision, and does the user say it helped?
seed_study.what_to_observe: Two things, recorded separately, because they discharge two different thresholds. (a) A decision stated before the preview and restated after it, so a reversal or a hardened confirmation is OBSERVED rather than self-reported; entertainment with no decision movement is kill criterion 3. (b) A direct question afterwards — did seeing it make you more or less confident about buying this, or about wearing it — because the confidence threshold is a STATED preference and observed behavior cannot stand in for it. Recording only (a) would let a completed study promote the confidence gate without ever collecting what its statement asks for.
discharges: Most users say the preview increased their purchase or wearing confidence.
It confirms, changes or vetoes a decision rather than being merely entertaining.

seed_study.question: Which distortions destroy trust immediately?
seed_study.what_to_observe: The first thing the user names as wrong, and whether they keep using the render after saying it. Ranked failure modes are what a provider choice is actually made on.
discharges: Most seed users say the render basically looks like them.
Most seed users find garment color and overall silhouette believable.

fit_accuracy_claim.decision: Whether any size or fit accuracy claim may ever be made.
fit_accuracy_claim.why_human: V3_SPEC §21 forbids a pseudo-precise fit score and §20.6 treats a size misunderstanding as a kill criterion. The default answer is no.

flag_enablement.decision: Turning ENABLE_V3_PURCHASE_DECISION / ENABLE_V3_AVATAR / ENABLE_V3_STATIC_TRYON on in production.
flag_enablement.why_human: The rollout itself. All three stay off in committed configuration.

privacy_copy.decision: The final photo-consent and privacy wording shown before a photo is used.

provider_choice.decision: Which production static try-on provider to use, and at what per-generation price.
provider_choice.why_human: Spend and a third-party data processor. Development has only ever run the fake adapter.

retention_reduction.decision: Any destructive migration or reduction of the photo/render retention policy.

seed_cohort.decision: Whether to recruit Phase 1 seed users and process their real photos.
seed_cohort.why_human: Development loops are forbidden from sending real user photos to a provider (workspace CLAUDE.md), so the first real-photo run is a human decision.

spending_budget.decision: The per-user and per-day generation budget, and the ceiling that stops a rollout.
spending_budget.why_human: A budget is a business commitment; the cost guard can enforce one but must not invent it.

telemetry_sink.decision: Which analytics sink receives V3 events, with what retention.
telemetry_sink.why_human: A third-party processor for behavioral data, plus a retention period with privacy consequences. Until it is chosen, every panel on this dashboard is empty.
